major_events.event: Over a thousand surviving heavenly monarchs seek refuge in the Yuan Realm, formally recognizing Fang Han as their master.
The Gate of Eternal Life fully manifests, spraying the first wave of rare divine materials and medicines.
Ying Tianqing is revealed as the reincarnation of the ancient Qingyi Immortal King, appearing in the void to seize sprayed items.
The Gate of Eternal Life initiates a second spray, unleashing numerous ancient characters alongside materials.
Hua Tiandu attacks Fang Han in rage to seize characters, but is easily repelled by a single punch.
Fang Han detonates the barrier protecting the opposing force, kills Ying Tianqing, and refines his essence into the Epoch Divine Array.
Fang Han purifies Tianfei Wumo and slays the seven ancient god emperors, forging the Seven Divine Swords as a defensive asset.
A massive parent Three Life Stone is sprayed, prompting a magnetic struggle between Fang Han and Hua Tiandu's child stone.
Fang Han's ocean avatar detonates itself inside Tiandu City, forcing Hua Tiandu to blood-sacrifice all his allied heavenly monarchs.
Fang Han employs the Natural Axe to crush Hua Tiandu's Universe Gourd, securing the parent Three Life Stone.
A toxic tumor is ejected from the Gate of Eternal Life under the influence of the Primordial Lord, merging with Hua Tiandu to make him an Immortal King.
Fang Han recognizes his true past life as the Gate's weapon spirit, breaks through to the Immortal King level, and absorbs the Dao character.
Eight liberated immortal kings emerge from the Gate of Eternal Life, throwing their support behind Hua Tiandu to counter Fang Han.
Three allied immortal kings friendly to Fang Han escape the Gate of Eternal Life to assist him.
Fang Han defeats Ciyuan Immortal King and shatters Shenhua Old Man's mirror, dominating the initial battlefield.
Fang Han extracts Hua Tiandu's origin, consumes his soul with the character 'Eat', and permanently erases him.
造化仙王 reveals his identity as Bai Haichan, presenting a binding karmic link that prevents Fang Han from creating a new era.
Fang Han offers the opposing immortal kings a free strike to resolve the karmic debt, resulting in his physical disintegration.

major_events.event: Fang Han resurrects from the Gate of Eternal Life, transcends the Immortal King level, and systematically slays the hostile kings.
造化仙王 voluntarily dissolves into smoke, and Fang Han leads his followers into the Gate to start the eternal era.

long_form_mechanisms.description: Allows Fang Han to shield his followers from cosmic decay and simulate the aura of an Immortal King prior to his actual breakthrough.
The World Tree acts as a cosmic magnet, drawing sprayed items from the Gate of Eternal Life into the Yuan Realm.
A smaller child stone can override the seal on a larger parent stone through a resonant attraction, pulling it away.
Sacrificing thousands of monarchs to instantly convert their laws and essence into personal power, bypassing normal cultivation.
The toxic tumor serves as the antithesis of the Gate, capable of corroding the energy of eternal life and elevating the host.
Integrating ancient characters from the Gate grants foundational laws, with the Dao character acting as the general outline for all characters.
Choosing not to resist a fatal blow from a creator pays the debt of guidance, dissolving karmic ties and triggering a stronger resurrection.

continuity_observations.observation: Chapter numbering contains an explicit typographical error in the sequence (第1627章 is followed by 第1228章, and then 第1629章).
The revelation that 造化仙王 is Bai Haichan resolves the initial plot point regarding the protagonist's mortal-world mentor from the novel's beginning.
Key long-standing characters such as Disaster and Chaos are killed not by Fang Han, but by the betrayal of their own leader, Hua Tiandu.
The text references the historical destruction of the World Tree by the Ancestral Saint King and his subsequent backlash.
The text lists eight opposing immortal kings initially, but later refers to ten when active combat commences.
Cultivation scaling undergoes massive inflation, where the protagonist jumps from 19 to 30 epochs in a brief sequence.
The character 'Eat' is used as a literal narrative mechanism to consume and erase the rival's soul.
Even when the Gate of Eternal Life is stabilized externally by the Primordial Lord, Fang Han's internal status as the spirit overrides the block.

style_observations.description: Frequent repetition of the phrase '诸王不是万能，而我无所不能' (Kings are not omnipotent, but I am omnipotent) to solidify the protagonist's status.
Usage of science-inspired terms like 'light-years' and 'billions' to describe sizes of weapons, stones, and entities.
Relying on standard xianxia terms like '化为飞灰' (turned to ashes) and '化为粉末' (turned to powder) to describe defeated foes.
Comparing highly ranked opposing kings to 'dogs' or 'eggs' to emphasize their sudden insignificance.
Direct explanations by the narrator detailing the backstories and secret motives of characters.
Vivid coloring of magical objects, such as the Seven Divine Swords flashing with seven specific blood hues.

originality_risks.description: The concept of allowing oneself to be killed by a creator to resolve karma and return stronger is a widely used trope in traditional mythology and fantasy.
originality_risks.anchor: 第1633章 给你们一个机会

originality_risks.description: Reducing the global conflict to a pre-destined binary between the cosmic spirit (good) and the cosmic tumor (bad) simplifies the character struggle.
The rapid jumps in epoch counts at the very end of the novel can feel like a rushed power creep to bring the story to a swift close.
Long-established rivals and powerful monarchs are quickly swept aside as raw fuel or minor obstacles to showcase the protagonist's growth.
